findings.title: Redis OSS 7.1 cache is supported; Valkey 9 recommended to cut cost
findings.description:
aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster sets engine = "redis" (main.tf:16) and engine_version = var.redis_version (main.tf:17), default "7.1" (variables.tf:14). Status: SUPPORTED (source: AWS documentation lifecycle table; live data and AWS Health not read because live_access=off). Redis OSS 7.0/7.1 is not in the Extended Support schedule for 4/5/6, so no Extended Support charges apply. Optional: move to Valkey for the lower price. Risk Medium (score 3): single-node cluster (+2), no test or staging environment found (+1). Severity stays Low because the cache is supported. Blocker: the resource is a standalone aws_elasticache_cluster, which can't cross-engine upgrade; refactor into an aws_elasticache_replication_group first (see F2). Node type default cache.t2.micro: confirm the node type is offered for the chosen Valkey version in the Region (DescribeCacheEngineVersions / AWS supported node types page) before the upgrade. Recommended version 9.1 comes from the AWS documentation; confirm the newest Valkey 9.x in the Region with DescribeCacheEngineVersions.

findings.title: Standalone aws_elasticache_cluster (engine redis) can't cross-engine upgrade
findings.description: aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster has no replication_group_id and engine = "redis". A single-node cluster can't be upgraded in place from Redis OSS to Valkey. Proposed manual change (separate change, not automated): refactor the module to an aws_elasticache_replication_group (for example num_cache_clusters >= 2 with automatic_failover_enabled and multi_az_enabled for production), migrate the data (snapshot restore or online migration), then rerun this analysis. Staying on Redis OSS 7.1 (target C) needs no change today.

findings.title: Warning: transit_encryption_enabled is unset (Terraform, Valkey target)
findings.description: The resource does not set transit_encryption_enabled. The AWS provider documents it as optional; whether the service accepts an in-place Redis to Valkey change without TLS isn't confirmed in the docs. Turning on TLS changes how every client connects. Don't enable it automatically: decide explicitly, and verify with terraform plan before applying.

findings.title: Warning: at_rest_encryption_enabled is unset (Terraform, Valkey target)
findings.description: at_rest_encryption_enabled is not set. aws_elasticache_cluster does not expose it, but the replication group the blocker refactor would create does, and the provider default differs by engine (false for redis, true for valkey). Require a real terraform plan before apply; if it shows a change to at_rest_encryption_enabled or transit_encryption_enabled, or any -/+ replacement, stop and set the attribute explicitly to the live value.

findings.title: Live data, AWS Health and Trusted Advisor not used (live_access=off)
findings.description: live_access=off was set, so no AWS calls were made. Status comes from the AWS documentation lifecycle table and the repository. Deployment state, live engine version, drift, unmanaged caches and Global Datastore membership could not be checked. The module has no callers in this repository, so the Region (var.region) and instance name (var.name) are unresolved. Rerun with read-only access (elasticache:Describe*, elasticache:ListTagsForResource, health:Describe*, support:DescribeTrustedAdvisor*, sts:GetCallerIdentity) to confirm.
